title: Prawn Chowder
subtitle: New England-style seafood chowder
excerpt: A creamy, hearty chowder of king prawns and potato in a rich milk and cream broth with leeks and thyme. It is warming and filling in the style of the classic New England clam chowder, built here with widely available prawns.
sourceNotes: New England clam chowder has been a staple of the American east coast since at least the eighteenth century. This version adapts the technique to king prawns, which are more accessible than live clams, while preserving the defining characteristics of the creamy, potato-thickened base.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The chowder base can be made up to the point of adding the prawns, then refrigerated. Add the prawns and cream when reheating.

content.text: The flour is cooked in the butter for a couple of minutes to form a roux before the liquid is added. This is what gives the chowder its thick, velvet-like body. Add the prawns in the last 3 to 4 minutes of cooking; they cook quickly and will turn rubbery if left in the heat too long.
Melt the butter in the saucepan over a medium heat. Cook the onion and leek for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Scatter in the flour and stir for 2 minutes so it cooks out and coats the vegetables.
Gradually pour in the milk, stirring constantly to prevent lumps forming. Add the bay leaves and diced potato.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potato is soft.
Stir in the double cream and the king prawns. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until the prawns are pink and just cooked through. Remove the bay leaves.
Season generously with salt and white pepper. Ladle into bowls and scatter over the parsley. Serve with crusty bread.

items.cause: The milk was added too quickly to the roux.
items.fix: Add milk gradually, stirring constantly, to create a smooth base.

items.cause: They were overcooked or went in too early.
items.fix: Add prawns in the last 3 to 4 minutes; remove when pink.

items.cause: Flour was not cooked long enough to thicken properly.
items.fix: Cook roux for 2 full minutes before adding any liquid.
